content.text: {"decision":"YES","supporting_policy_ids":["E01","E02","E03","E04","E05","E06","E07","E08","E09","E10","E11","E12","E13"],"missing_facts":[],"justification":"All policy requirements are met for the £120 donation (FP-0316-EL) from Elaine Carter on 16 March 2026. (1) The charity is recognised by HMRC for tax purposes, confirmed by the 2023 recognition letter and status check as of 16 March 2026 [E02]. (2) The donation is from an individual (Elaine Carter, personal current account) [E06]. (3) Elaine paid £980 in Income Tax in the 2025-26 tax year, which comfortably exceeds the £80 total Gift Aid to be reclaimed across all her donations that year (£30 on this donation plus £50 on others), satisfying the tax-paid requirement [E04, E07]. (4) Elaine signed an electronic Gift Aid declaration on 15 March 2026, covering this donation, with a full audit trail [E05]. (5) None of the exclusions apply: the payment came directly from Elaine's personal bank account (not Payroll Giving [E09]); it is not a payment for goods or services and no benefit was provided to Elaine beyond a standard thank-you email [E10, E11]; no shares or securities were involved [E12]; and although an older spreadsheet groups it with CAF card/voucher redemptions (CC-0314, VC-0317), FP-0316-EL is demonstrably a direct bank transfer from Elaine received on 16 March, not a charity card or voucher redemption — those were separate transactions settled in a combined batch on 18 March [E13]. The treasurer may therefore include FP-0316-EL in the ordinary Gift Aid return and reclaim 25p per £1, i.e. £30 on this donation.","scope_issues":[],"conditional_branches":[]}
